instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls?
response: A strength exercise for the biceps, done with dumbbells. How to do it: Hold the dumbbell towards the side farther from you so that you have more weight on the side closest to you. (This can be done for a good effect on all bicep dumbbell exercises). Now do a normal incline dumbbell curl, but keep your wrists as far back as possible so as to neutralize any stress that is placed on them. Sit on an incline bench that is angled at 45-degrees while holding a dumbbell on each hand. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

input: How do I do the Dumbbell Side Bend?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done with dumbbells. How to do it: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist. Your feet should be placed at shoulder width. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Can you explain how to do the Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the abdominals, done using a medicine ball. It also works the chest, lats and shoulders. How to do it: Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent. Hold the ball with one hand, extending the arm fully behind your head. This will be your starting position. Initiate the movement at the shoulder, throwing the ball directly forward of you as you sit up, attempting to go for maximum distance. The ball can be thrown to a partner or bounced off of a wall. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

input: Can you explain how to do the Cuban Press?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done with dumbbells. It also works the traps. How to do it: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position. To initiate the movement, externally rotate the shoulders to move the upper arm 180 degrees. Keep the upper arms in place, rotating the upper arms until the wrists are directly above the elbows, the forearms perpendicular to the floor. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Kettlebell Figure 8 safely?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a kettlebell. It also works the hamstrings and shoulders. How to do it: Place one kettlebell between your legs and take a wider than shoulder width stance. Bend over by pushing your butt out and keeping your back flat. Pick up a kettlebell and pass it to your other hand between your legs. The receiving hand should reach from behind the legs. Go back and forth for several repetitions. Safety tip: Keep a neutral spine, drive the movement from your hips and legs, and clear space around you.

input: quick question: what is progressive overload?
response: Progressive overload means gradually asking your body to do a bit more over time so it keeps adapting. instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for One-Arm Kettlebell Row?
response: A strength exercise for the middle back, done using a kettlebell. It also works the biceps and lats. How to do it: Place a kettlebell in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position. Grab the kettlebell and pull it to your stomach, retracting your shoulder blade and flexing the elbow. Keep your back straight. Lower and repeat. Safety tip: Keep a neutral spine, drive the movement from your hips and legs, and clear space around you.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning?
response: A strength exercise for the lower back, done using a barbell. It also works the glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it. Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.

response: Overtraining (or more commonly under-recovery) happens when training stress outpaces recovery. Signs include lasting fatigue, falling performance, poor sleep, irritability, frequent illness, and soreness that doesn't go away. Take a few easier days or a deload week, prioritise sleep and food, and see a doctor if symptoms continue.
context: Guidance (Signs of overtraining): Persistent fatigue, falling performance, poor sleep, irritability, frequent illness and lingering soreness can mean training load is higher than recovery allows. Reducing volume or taking a lighter week (a deload) usually helps.

Guidance (Progressive overload): Progressive overload means gradually increasing the challenge: a little more weight, an extra rep, an extra set, or better control. When you can complete the top of your rep range with good form for all sets, increase the weight slightly.

input: Can you explain how to do the Close-Grip Push-Up off of a Dumbbell?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done with no equipment. It also works the abdominals, chest and shoulders. How to do it: Lie on the floor and place your hands on an upright dumbbell. Supporting your weight on your toes and hands, keep your torso rigid and your elbows in with your arms straight. This will be your starting position. Lower your body, allowing the elbows to flex while you inhale. Keep your body straight, not allowing your hips to rise or sag. Press yourself back up to the starting position by extending the elbows. Breathe out as you perform this step. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

response: A dynamic plank-position exercise that trains the core and raises the heart rate. How to do it: Begin in a pushup position, with your weight supported by your hands and toes. input: How do I do the Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench?

input: What is DOMS?
response: That's likely delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), which is common after new or harder exercise and usually peaks 24-72 hours later. It fades on its own. response: Overtraining (or more commonly under-recovery) happens when training stress outpaces recovery. Signs include lasting fatigue, falling performance, poor sleep, irritability, frequent illness, and soreness that doesn't go away. Take a few easier days or a deload week, prioritise sleep and food, and see a doctor if symptoms continue.

input: what does reps in reserve mean pls

what does reps in reserve mean pls

Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done at the end of a set - 2 RIR means you stopped two reps before failure. RPE is a 1-10 effort scale, where RPE 8 roughly equals 2 reps in reserve. Most working sets should land around 1-3 RIR (RPE 7-9).

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Seated Hamstring safely?
response: A stretch for the hamstrings, done with no equipment. It also works the calves. How to do it: In a seated position with your legs extended, have your partner stand behind you. Now, lean forward as your partner braces your shoulders with their hands. This will be your starting position. Attempt to push your torso back for 10-20 seconds, as your partner prevents any actual movement of your torso. Now relax your muscles as your partner increases the stretch by gently pushing your torso forward for 10-20 seconds. Safety tip: Stretch to mild tension only, breathe slowly, and never bounce or force the position.

input: What's the proper form for Shoulder Press?
response: An overhead press that builds the deltoids and triceps. How to do it: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, sit on a military press bench or utility bench that has back support. Place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs. Now raise the dumbbells to shoulder height one at a time using your thighs to help propel them up into position. Safety tip: Brace your core, avoid arching your lower back and press in a controlled path without locking out aggressively.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Drag Curl?
response: A strength exercise for the biceps, done using a barbell. It also works the forearms. How to do it: Grab a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward) and get your elbows close to your torso and back. This will be your starting position. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

How to do it: With a dumbbell in each hand (palms facing your torso), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward by bending at the waist; as you bend make sure to keep your back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. Safety tip: Hinge at the hips with a neutral spine and keep the weight moderate until the position feels stable.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Split Jump?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the quadriceps, done with no equipment. It also works the calves, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: Assume a lunge stance position with one foot forward with the knee bent, and the rear knee nearly touching the ground. Ensure that the front knee is over the midline of the foot. Extending through both legs, jump as high as possible, swinging your arms to gain lift. As you jump, bring your feet together, and move them back to their initial positions as you land. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Pallof Press With Rotation safely?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a cable machine. It also works the chest, shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and position the cable to shoulder height. With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Align outstretched arm with cable. With your feet positioned hip-width apart, pull the cable into your chest and grab the handle with your other hand. Both hands should be on the handle at this time. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

input: How do I perform Lying Close-Grip Barbell Triceps Press To Chin with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done using an ez curl bar. How to do it: While holding a barbell or EZ Curl bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward), lie on your back on a flat bench with your head off the end of the bench. Tip: If you are holding a barbell grab it using a shoulder-width grip and if you are using an E-Z Bar grab it on the inner handles. Extend your arms in front of you as you hold the barbell over your chest. The arms should be perpendicular to your torso (90-degree angle). This will be your starting position. Safety tip: Keep your elbows steady and your back neutral, and start with a load you can lift without swinging.

input: Tips for doing the Barbell Full Squat safely?
response: A strength exercise for the quadriceps, done using a barbell. It also works the calves, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Crossover Reverse Lunge safely?
response: A stretch for the lower back, done with no equipment. It also works the abdominals, abductors and glutes. How to do it: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position. Perform a rear lunge by stepping back with one foot and flexing the hips and front knee. As you do so, rotate your torso across the front leg. After a brief pause, return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, continuing in an alternating fashion. Safety tip: Stretch to mild tension only, breathe slowly, and never bounce or force the position.

response: A strength exercise for the biceps, done using an ez curl bar. How to do it: Stand up straight while holding an EZ curl bar at the wide outer handle. input: How do I perform Push Up to Side Plank with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the chest, done with no equipment. It also works the abdominals, shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Get into pushup position on the toes with your hands just outside of shoulder width. Perform a pushup by allowing the elbows to flex. As you descend, keep your body straight. Lower the arm back to the floor for another pushup and then twist to the other side. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Cable Reverse Crunch?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a cable machine. How to do it: Connect an ankle strap attachment to a low pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it. Sit down with your feet toward the pulley and attach the cable to your ankles. Lie down, elevate your legs and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle. Your legs and the cable should be aligned. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are. With your hands behind your head, bring your knees inward to your torso and elevate your hips off the floor. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Leg Extension safely?
response: A machine isolation exercise for the quadriceps. How to do it: For this exercise you will need to use a leg extension machine. First choose your weight and sit on the machine with your legs under the pad (feet pointed forward) and the hands holding the side bars. This will be your starting position. Tip: You will need to adjust the pad so that it falls on top of your lower leg (just above your feet). Also, make sure that your legs form a 90-degree angle between the lower and upper leg. If the angle is less than 90-degrees then that means the knee is over the toes which in turn creates undue stress at the knee joint. If the machine is designed that way, either look for another machine or just make sure that when you start executing the exercise you stop going down once you hit the 90-degree angle. Safety tip: Adjust the pad to sit just above your ankles and lift with control rather than kicking.

input: How do I do the Seated Leg Tucks?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done with no equipment. How to do it: Sit on a bench with the legs stretched out in front of you slightly below parallel and your arms holding on to the sides of the bench. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

How to do it: Adjust the machine lever to fit your height and lie face down on the leg curl machine with the pad of the lever on the back of your legs (just a few inches under the calves). Safety tip: Keep your hips pressed into the pad and avoid jerking the weight.

input: How do I perform Russian Twists with good form?
response: A rotational core exercise that targets the obliques. How to do it: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Safety tip: Rotate through your upper back with control; keep your feet on the floor if you feel strain in your lower back.

A gradual rate of about 0.5-1 kg (1-2 lb) per week is easier to maintain.

input: Tips for doing the Advanced Kettlebell Windmill safely?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a kettlebell. It also works the glutes, hamstrings and shoulders. How to do it: Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm. Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Keep the non-working arm behind your back and turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the kettlebell. Lower yourself as far as possible. Pause for a second and reverse the motion back to the starting position. Safety tip: Keep a neutral spine, drive the movement from your hips and legs, and clear space around you.

Guidance (Pain vs normal effort): Muscle burning during a set and mild next-day soreness are normal. response: Alcohol adds calories, can disrupt sleep and may slow recovery and muscle repair, especially in larger amounts. Guidance (Hydration during exercise): Drink fluids before, during and after exercise, especially in heat. For most workouts under an hour, water is enough. For long or very sweaty sessions, fluids with electrolytes and carbohydrates can help. Drinking excessive amounts of plain water during very long events can be dangerous, so drink to thirst rather than forcing fluids.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
response: Calorie needs vary a lot with age, size, sex and activity, so there's no single number. A practical approach is to estimate your maintenance intake (for example with a reputable online calculator or by tracking your current intake while your weight is stable) and eat about 300-500 calories less per day, then adjust based on progress. Avoid very low intakes; if you have a medical condition, ask a doctor or registered dietitian for a personalised target.
context: Guidance (Safe rate of weight loss): Gradual weight loss of about 0.5 to 1 kg (1 to 2 pounds) per week is more likely to be maintained. Crash diets, very low calorie intakes and skipping meals are hard to sustain and can lead to muscle loss and nutrient shortfalls.

Guidance (Exercise for weight loss): Combining aerobic activity with strength training supports fat loss while helping preserve muscle. Many people need more than 150 minutes per week of moderate activity to lose weight and keep it off. Diet changes usually have the bigger effect on the calorie deficit.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Chest Push with Run Release with good form?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the chest, done using a medicine ball. It also works the abdominals, shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Begin in an athletic stance with the knees bent, hips back, and back flat. Hold the medicine ball near your legs. This will be your starting position. While taking your first step draw the medicine ball into your chest. As you take the second step, explosively push the ball forward, immediately sprinting for 10 yards after the release. If you are really fast, you can catch your own pass! Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

input: Tips for doing the Muscle Up safely?
response: A strength exercise for the lats, done with other. It also works the abdominals, biceps and forearms. How to do it: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings. Initiate a pull up by pulling the elbows down to your side, flexing the elbows. As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement. Safety tip: Learn the movement with a light load first and make sure the equipment is stable and secure.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Barbell Curl with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the biceps, done using a barbell. It also works the forearms. How to do it: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position. While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Incline Press?
response: A pressing movement on an inclined bench that emphasises the upper chest and front shoulders. How to do it: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand atop your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other. Then, using your thighs to help push the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them at shoulder width. Once you have the dumbbells raised to shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position. Safety tip: Set the bench to a moderate incline (about 30-45 degrees) and keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.

input: How do I do the Goblet Squat?
response: A squat holding one dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest, which naturally encourages an upright torso. How to do it: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. Safety tip: Hold the weight close to your chest and keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Single-Arm Linear Jammer?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a barbell. It also works the chest and triceps. How to do it: Position a bar into a landmine or securely anchor it in a corner. Load the bar to an appropriate weight. Raise the bar from the floor, taking it to your shoulders with one or both hands. Adopt a wide stance. This will be your starting position. Perform the movement by extending the elbow, pressing the weight up. Move explosively, extending the hips and knees fully to produce maximal force. Return to the starting position. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

input: What's the best way to lose weight?
response: Weight loss comes from a sustained, modest calorie deficit. Practical steps: base meals on vegetables, fruit, lean protein and whole grains; include protein at every meal to stay full; limit sugary drinks and highly processed snacks; watch portion sizes; aim for at least 150 minutes of activity a week plus 2 strength sessions; and sleep 7+ hours. A gradual rate of about 0.5-1 kg (1-2 lb) per week is easier to maintain.

Guidance (Exercise for weight loss): Combining aerobic activity with strength training supports fat loss while helping preserve muscle. Many people need more than 150 minutes per week of moderate activity to lose weight and keep it off. Diet changes usually have the bigger effect on the calorie deficit.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher safely?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done using a barbell. It also works the chest and shoulders. How to do it: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench. Using a close grip (a grip that is slightly less than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked and elbows in. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position. Tip: In order to protect your rotator cuff, it is best if you have a spotter help you lift the barbell off the rack. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Band Skull Crusher?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done with resistance bands. How to do it: Secure a band to the base of a rack or the bench. Lay on the bench so that the band is lined up with your head. Take hold of the band, raising your elbows so that the upper arm is perpendicular to the floor. With the elbow flexed, the band should be above your head. This will be your starting position. Extend through the elbow to straighten your arm, keeping your upper arm in place. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position. Safety tip: Check the band for nicks or tears before use and anchor it securely so it cannot snap back.

Guidance (Muscle soreness (DOMS)): Delayed-onset muscle soreness usually peaks 24 to 72 hours after new or harder exercise and fades on its own. Gentle movement, sleep, hydration and adequate protein help. Sharp pain, swelling, or pain that does not improve is different from soreness and should be checked by a professional.

response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the adductors, done with no equipment. It also works the abdominals, abductors and calves. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

response: A strength exercise for the lats, done using a cable machine. It also works the biceps and middle back. How to do it: Attach a single handle to a low cable. Clasp your hands behind your head, beginning with your shoulder blades on the ground. This will be your starting position. Perform the motion by flexing the spine and rotating your torso to bring the left elbow to the right knee. Return to the starting position and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

input: quick question: what is dynamic stretching?
response: Dynamic stretching uses controlled movement through a range - leg swings, arm circles, walking lunges - and is ideal for warming up. Static stretching holds a position still for 15-30 seconds and is better after workouts or in separate flexibility sessions.
context: Guidance (Dynamic vs static stretching): Dynamic stretches move joints through their range of motion and are best before exercise. Long static stretches are better after a workout or as a separate flexibility session, because very long static holds right before explosive or heavy efforts may slightly reduce performance.

Guidance (Static stretching guidance): For flexibility, stretch major muscle groups at least 2 to 3 days per week, holding each static stretch for about 10 to 30 seconds to the point of mild tension, not pain, and repeating 2 to 4 times. Do not bounce.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Isometric Chest Squeezes?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the chest, done with no equipment. It also works the shoulders and triceps. How to do it: While either seating or standing, bend your arms at a 90-degree angle and place the palms of your hands together in front of your chest. Tip: Your hands should be open with the palms together and fingers facing forward (perpendicular to your torso). Push both hands against each other as you contract your chest. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction. Hold for the recommended number of seconds. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

response: A stretch for the lats, done using a foam roller. How to do it: While lying on the floor, place a foam roll under your back and to one side, just behind your arm pit. input: Can you explain how to do the Double Kettlebell Jerk?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a kettlebell. It also works the calves, quadriceps and triceps. How to do it: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward. Safety tip: Keep a neutral spine, drive the movement from your hips and legs, and clear space around you.

input: How do I do the Dumbbell Seated Box Jump?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the quadriceps, done with dumbbells. It also works the calves, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: Position a box a couple feet to the side of a bench. Hold a dumbbell to your chest with both hands and seat yourself on the bench facing the box. This will be your starting position. Plant your feet firmly on the ground as you lean forward, extending through the hips and knees to jump up and forward. Land on the box with both feet, absorbing the impact by allowing the hips and knees to bend. Step down and return to the starting position. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Dip Machine?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done using a machine. It also works the chest and shoulders. How to do it: Sit securely in a dip machine, select the weight and firmly grasp the handles. Now keep your elbows in at your sides in order to place emphasis on the triceps. The elbows should be bent at a 90 degree angle. As you contract the triceps, extend your arms downwards as you exhale. Tip: At the bottom of the movement, focus on keeping a little bend in your arms to keep tension on the triceps muscle. Now slowly let your arms come back up to the starting position as you inhale. Safety tip: Adjust the seat and pads so the joint lines up with the machine's pivot, and move through a pain-free range.

How to do it: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip). This is the starting position. Safety tip: Keep a slight bend in the elbows, a flat back and use light weights.

response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the lats, done using a medicine ball. It also works the abdominals, chest and shoulders. How to do it: Begin standing while facing a wall or a partner. Using both hands, position the ball behind your head, stretching as much as possible, and forcefully throw the ball forward. Ensure that you follow your throw through, being prepared to receive your rebound from your throw. If you are throwing against the wall, make sure that you stand close enough to the wall to receive the rebound, and aim a little higher than you would with a partner. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Romanian Deadlift from Deficit?
response: An Olympic weightlifting movement for the hamstrings, done using a barbell. It also works the forearms, glutes and lower back. How to do it: Begin standing while holding a bar at arm's length in front of you. You can stand on a raised platform to increase the range of motion. Begin by flexing the knees slightly, and then flex at the hip, moving your butt back as far as possible, lowering the torso as far as flexibility allows. The back should remain in absolute extension at all times, and the bar should remain in contact with the legs. If done properly, there should be heavy tension felt in the hamstrings. Safety tip: This is a technical lift - learn it with a coach and an empty bar or PVC pipe before adding weight.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Smith Machine Leg Press with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the quadriceps, done using a machine. It also works the calves, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: Position a Smith machine bar a couple feet off of the ground. Ensure that it is resting on the safeties. After loading the bar to an appropriate weight, lie underneath the bar. Place the middle of your feet on the bar, tucking your knees to your chest. This will be your starting position. Begin the movement by driving through your feet to move the bar upward, extending the hips and knees. Do not lock out your knees. Safety tip: Adjust the seat and pads so the joint lines up with the machine's pivot, and move through a pain-free range.

response: A cable fly variation that keeps constant tension on the chest throughout the movement. How to do it: To get yourself into the starting position, place the pulleys on a high position (above your head), select the resistance to be used and hold the pulleys in each hand. input: What's the proper form for Reverse Barbell Preacher Curls?
response: A strength exercise for the biceps, done using an ez curl bar. It also works the forearms. How to do it: Grab an EZ-bar using a shoulder width and palms down (pronated) grip. Now place the upper part of both arms on top of the preacher bench and have your arms extended. This will be your starting position. As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbell is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position. Safety tip: Keep your elbows steady and your back neutral, and start with a load you can lift without swinging.

input: How do I do the Barbell Hack Squat?
response: A strength exercise for the quadriceps, done using a barbell. It also works the calves, forearms and hamstrings. How to do it: Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position. While keeping your head and eyes up and back straight, squat until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in as you slowly go down. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

input: Tips for doing the Medicine Ball Full Twist safely?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the abdominals, done using a medicine ball. It also works the shoulders. How to do it: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position. Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner. For full rotation, you and your partner should twist in the same direction, i.e. counter-clockwise. Pass the ball to your partner, and both of you can now twist in the opposite direction to repeat the procedure. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Ball Leg Curl safely?
response: A strength exercise for the hamstrings, done using an exercise ball. It also works the calves and glutes. How to do it: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball. Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position. Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet. Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings. Safety tip: Use a correctly inflated ball on a non-slip surface and start near a wall for balance.

People with diabetes or other conditions should follow their doctor's advice.

input: What's the proper form for Cable Crunch?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a cable machine. How to do it: Kneel below a high pulley that contains a rope attachment. Grasp cable rope attachment and lower the rope until your hands are placed next to your face. Flex your hips slightly and allow the weight to hyperextend the lower back. This will be your starting position. With the hips stationary, flex the waist as you contract the abs so that the elbows travel towards the middle of the thighs. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

input: What's the proper form for One-Arm Kettlebell Snatch?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a kettlebell. It also works the calves, glutes and hamstrings. How to do it: Place a kettlebell between your feet. Bend your knees and push your butt back to get in the proper starting position. Look straight ahead and swing the kettlebell back between your legs. A strength exercise for the abdominals, done using a cable machine. It also works the shoulders. How to do it: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and move the cable to the highest pulley position. With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball?
response: A strength exercise for the chest, done using an exercise ball. It also works the shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart from each other holding your torso up at arms length. Place your toes on top of an exercise ball. This will allow your body to be elevated. Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale. Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you perform this step. Safety tip: Use a correctly inflated ball on a non-slip surface and start near a wall for balance.

input: Tips for doing the Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension safely?
response: A strength exercise for the triceps, done with dumbbells. It also works the chest and shoulders. How to do it: Lie on a flat bench while holding two dumbbells directly in front of you. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

input: Tips for doing the One-Legged Cable Kickback safely?
response: A strength exercise for the glutes, done using a cable machine. It also works the hamstrings. How to do it: Hook a leather ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and then attach the cuff to your ankle. Face the weight stack from a distance of about two feet, grasping the steel frame for support. While keeping your knees and hips bent slightly and your abs tight, contract your glutes to slowly "kick" the working leg back in a semicircular arc as high as it will comfortably go as you breathe out. Tip: At full extension, squeeze your glutes for a second in order to achieve a peak contraction. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

input: What's the proper form for External Rotation with Cable?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a cable machine. How to do it: Adjust the cable to the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away. Grasp the handle with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position. With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I do the Dumbbell Press?
response: A chest press with dumbbells that allows a natural range of motion and trains each side independently. How to do it: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other. Safety tip: Choose a weight you can control, and bring the dumbbells to your chest before sitting up rather than dropping them to the sides.

input: Tips for doing the Hurdle Hops safely?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the hamstrings, done with other. It also works the abductors, adductors and calves. How to do it: Set up a row of hurdles or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart. Stand in front of the first hurdle with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position. Begin by jumping with both feet over the first hurdle, swinging both arms as you jump. Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next hurdle. Continue until you have jumped over all of the hurdles. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

input: Tips for doing the Standing Barbell Press Behind Neck safely?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done using a barbell. It also works the triceps. How to do it: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for easier pick up of the bar. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it. Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso. Safety tip: Use collars on the bar, warm up with lighter sets, and use a spotter or safety pins for heavy pressing or squatting.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Bottoms Up with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the abdominals, done with no equipment. How to do it: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms at your side. This will be your starting position. To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest by flexing the hips and knees. Following this, extend your legs directly above you so that they are perpendicular to the ground. Rotate and elevate your pelvis to raise your glutes from the floor. After a brief pause, return to the starting position. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Can you explain how to do the Lateral Bound?
response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the adductors, done with no equipment. It also works the abductors, calves and glutes. How to do it: Assume a half squat position facing 90 degrees from your direction of travel. This will be your starting position. Allow your lead leg to do a countermovement inward as you shift your weight to the outside leg. Immediately push off and extend, attempting to bound to the side as far as possible. Upon landing, immediately push off in the opposite direction, returning to your original start position. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Tips for doing the Seated Dumbbell Press safely?
response: A strength exercise for the shoulders, done with dumbbells. It also works the triceps. How to do it: Grab a couple of dumbbells and sit on a military press bench or an utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs. Clean the dumbbells up one at a time by using your thighs to bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height at each side. Rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. This is your starting position. As you exhale, push the dumbbells up until they touch at the top. Safety tip: Pick a weight you can control through the full range, and set the dumbbells down carefully rather than dropping them.

response: A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the quadriceps, done with no equipment. It also works the abductors, adductors and calves. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

Can you explain how to do the Stride Jump Crossover?

A plyometric (jumping/explosive) exercise for the quadriceps, done with other. It also works the abductors, adductors and calves. How to do it: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge. Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward. Land in the opposite position that you started, on the opposite side of the box. The foot that was initially on the box will now be on the ground, with the opposite foot now on the box. Repeat the movement, crossing back over to the other side. Safety tip: Land softly with knees tracking over the toes, and only add volume once your landings stay quiet and controlled.

input: Tips for doing the Incline Cable Chest Press safely?
response: A strength exercise for the chest, done using a cable machine. It also works the shoulders and triceps. How to do it: Adjust the weight to an appropriate amount and be seated, grasping the handles. Your upper arms should be about 45 degrees to the body, with your head and chest up. The elbows should be bent to about 90 degrees. This will be your starting position. Begin by extending through the elbow, pressing the handles together straight in front of you. Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you execute the movement. Safety tip: Check the pin is fully inserted and the attachment is secure, and control the weight on the way back.

input: Should I do cardio or strength training to lose fat?
response: Both help, and combining them works best. Diet usually has the biggest effect on the calorie deficit, so pair a sensible eating plan with 2-3 strength sessions and regular cardio.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How do I perform Glute Kickback with good form?
response: A strength exercise for the glutes, done with no equipment. It also works the hamstrings. How to do it: Kneel on the floor or an exercise mat and bend at the waist with your arms extended in front of you (perpendicular to the torso) in order to get into a kneeling push-up position but with the arms spaced at shoulder width. Your head should be looking forward and the bend of the knees should create a 90-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves. This will be your starting position. Safety tip: Move with control, keep good alignment, and use an easier variation if you cannot keep your form.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: How long does it take muscles to recover?
response: Most muscle groups recover from a hard session in about 48-72 hours, depending on training volume, sleep and nutrition. That's why many plans train each muscle group 2 times a week with a day or two between. Lighter sessions need less recovery.
context: Guidance (Rest days): Muscles adapt between sessions, not during them. Most people benefit from at least 1 to 2 rest days per week and about 48 hours before training the same muscle group hard again. Light walking or mobility work on rest days (active recovery) is fine.

Guidance (Muscle soreness (DOMS)): Delayed-onset muscle soreness usually peaks 24 to 72 hours after new or harder exercise and fades on its own. Gentle movement, sleep, hydration and adequate protein help. Sharp pain, swelling, or pain that does not improve is different from soreness and should be checked by a professional.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: What's the proper form for Lower Back-SMR?
response: A stretch for the lower back, done using a foam roller. How to do it: In a seated position, place a foam roll under your lower back. Cross your arms in front of you and protract your shoulders. This will be your starting position. Raise your hips off of the floor and lean back, keeping your weight on your lower back. Now shift your weight slightly to one side, keeping your weight off of the spine and on the muscles to the side of it. Roll over your lower back, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other side. Safety tip: Stretch to mild tension only, breathe slowly, and never bounce or force the position.

instruction: You are FitBot, a fitness assistant.
input: Is it normal to feel tierd after working out?
response: Feeling pleasantly tired after a hard workout is normal. Extreme exhaustion, or fatigue that lasts into the next days, often means the session was too hard, or you're short on sleep, food or fluids. Ease the intensity, eat a balanced meal with protein and carbs after training, and rest well. See a doctor if tiredness is persistent or unusual.
context: Guidance (Signs of overtraining): Persistent fatigue, falling performance, poor sleep, irritability, frequent illness and lingering soreness can mean training load is higher than recovery allows. Reducing volume or taking a lighter week (a deload) usually helps.

Guidance (Muscle soreness (DOMS)): Delayed-onset muscle soreness usually peaks 24 to 72 hours after new or harder exercise and fades on its own. Gentle movement, sleep, hydration and adequate protein help. Sharp pain, swelling, or pain that does not improve is different from soreness and should be checked by a professional.
